title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework AI RMF 1.0
key_claim: AI RMF is a voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific and use-case-agnostic framework for organisations designing, developing, deploying or using AI systems.
limitations: US framework; not law; requires local adaptation.
notes: Core governance anchor for risk framing.

title: AI Risk Management Framework
key_claim: NIST AI RMF supports trustworthy AI risk management across design, development, use and evaluation of AI products, services and systems.
limitations: Framework source; implementation detail still needs local translation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Playbook for the UK Government
key_claim: The UK AI Playbook includes principles covering limitations, lawful and responsible use, secure use, meaningful human control, lifecycle management and assurance.
limitations: Government-focused; must be translated carefully for SMEs and non-public organisations.
notes: Strong source for practical governance language.

title: SME Digital Adoption Taskforce final report
key_claim: The DBT taskforce report focuses on supporting SMEs to adopt productivity-enhancing digital technologies including cloud, CRM, resource planning and AI tools.
limitations: Industry-led taskforce; policy recommendations rather than neutral academic study.
notes: Strong source for SME adoption barriers and support model.

title: SME Digital Adoption Taskforce final report HTML
key_claim: The final report provides practical steps and recommendations to enhance SME digital technology adoption.
limitations: Government policy context; detailed claims require close extraction before quotation.
notes: Detailed source page for SME recommendations.

title: AI and Data Protection Risk Toolkit
key_claim: The ICO toolkit helps organisations reduce AI-related risks to individuals' rights and freedoms.
limitations: ICO guidance may be updated; check freshness before final publication.

title: Guidelines for secure AI system development
key_claim: AI systems should be developed, deployed and operated securely across secure design, development, deployment, operation and maintenance.
limitations: Primarily provider/developer-facing; translate for non-technical adopters.

title: Make the service simple to use
key_claim: Simple services help users succeed first time and reduce mistakes, support demand and trust damage.
limitations: Public-service framing; translate carefully for SMEs and internal workflows.
notes: Supports admin-burden mapping and failure-demand language.

title: Provide a joined up experience across all channels
key_claim: Joined-up channels reduce workarounds and allow staff to spend less time on failure demand.
limitations: Public-service framing; useful across multi-channel admin workflows.
notes: Useful for enquiry and intake patterns.

title: Administrative simplification
key_claim: Administrative simplification reduces bureaucratic complexity; digital tools and AI can help, but procedures should be simplified first.
limitations: Topic page rather than single empirical study; use as conceptual framing.

title: The Digital Transformation of SMEs
key_claim: SMEs can gain from digitalisation through automation and better intelligence but smaller firms lag because of resource, awareness, skills and finance constraints.
limitations: 2021 source; pair with newer UK evidence before final claims.

title: OECD AI Principles
key_claim: Trustworthy AI should respect human rights, democratic values, transparency, explainability, robustness, security and accountability.
limitations: Principles-level guidance rather than implementation playbook.
